name: attack-outcomes
intro: The attack outcomes a risk scenario names: what the attacker is after, how the attack ends (the ATT&CK tactic whose success realizes the outcome), a reference dwell time (how long an attacker usually stays before it, a catalog value the price does not read), which security criteria of the primary asset the outcome breaches, and its techniques. Each technique gets a weight: the share of the outcome's relevant threats whose repertoire holds it, whatever its column. With no relevant threat, a signature technique weighs 0.5 and a related one 0.2: the only place where the two columns differ. A technique neither list holds joins them when at least 2 relevant threats use it with a weight of at least 0.3, 10 at most. The techniques that weigh more than 0 link the outcome's scenarios to the controls that cover them. The attack run that prices a scenario does not walk this list: it plays the whole repertoires of the relevant threats, and does not run without at least one. Every tenant gets this catalog at boot.
